previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old female with a history of type I diabetes, end-stage renal disease with prior kidney and pancreas transplants, and severe mitral regurgitation was admitted for worsening heart failure symptoms. She underwent elective coronary artery bypass grafting x3 and mechanical mitral valve replacement. The surgery was performed due to severe three-vessel coronary disease and ischemic mitral regurgitation. She tolerated the procedure well, was extubated on postoperative day one, and transitioned to the telemetry floor. Her renal function remained stable throughout admission, and she was managed on warfarin for mechanical valve anticoagulation. By discharge on postoperative day six, she was ambulating with assistance, pain was controlled with oral medications, and incisions were healing. She was discharged to an extended care facility for rehabilitation with detailed instructions on wound care, activity restrictions, and medication management.

radiology_notes.text:
CT CHEST, ___.

Comparison chest CT ___ and comparison chest x-ray of ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Volumetric, multidetector CT of the chest was performed without
intravenous or oral contrast.  Images are presented for display in the axial
plane at 5-mm and 1.25-mm collimation.  A series of multiplanar reformation
images were also submitted for review.

FINDINGS:  Large left pleural effusion is present, occupying nearly the
entirety of the left hemithorax with associated rightward shift of the
mediastinum, inversion of the left hemidiaphragm, and atelectasis of the left
upper and lower lobes with only a small amount of residual aerated lung within
the superior segment left lower lobe and apex of the left upper lobe. 
Hounsfield units of the pleural effusion are slightly greater than simple
fluid, measuring about 20 Hounsfield units.  On the right, a small dependent
pleural effusion has decreased in size from the prior CT and has Hounsfield
units consistent with simple fluid, approximately 2.  The patient is status
post median sternotomy and mitral valve surgery.  Pericardial effusion is
small to moderate in size and new from the preoperative CT of ___.  Heart is mildly enlarged and diffuse coronary artery calcifications are
again visualized.  Small round fluid collection in the right anterior
mediastinum measuring 1.6 cm is new from the preoperative CT and has a tubular
longitudinal configuration.  This is not fully characterized without
intravenous contrast but could potentially represent fluid within the track of
a previous mediastinal drain in this location based on comparison postop chest
x-ray of ___.  A vascular abnormality is less likely but cannot be
excluded without intravenous contrast administration.

Within the aerated portions of the lungs, bilateral pattern of pulmonary edema
has resolved in the interval.

Exam was not specifically tailored to evaluate the subdiaphragmatic region,
but note is made of atrophy of the right kidney and diffuse vascular
calcifications throughout the abdominal aorta and its branches including the
renal arteries.  The left kidney is not imaged but was previously shown to be
atrophic.  Soft tissue structures are remarkable for mild anasarca.

Sternal wires appear intact.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Large left pleural effusion is similar to recent chest x-ray of ___ but substantially larger compared to earlier postoperative radiographs of
___.  Hounsfield units are slightly greater than simple fluid and could
reflect complicated contents including prior hemorrhage, but there is no
evidence to suggest active bleeding into the pleural space.  The effusion is
associated with marked inversion of left hemidiaphragm as well as shift of
mediastinal structures towards the right.

2.  Resolution of pulmonary edema and decrease in size of right pleural
effusion since ___ left chest CT.

INDICATION:  Right-sided thoracentesis, evaluate for pneumothorax.  Background
of coronary artery bypass grafting and mitral valve replacement.

COMPARISON:  Radiographs dating back to ___ and most recently ___.

FINDINGS:  A moderately large left pleural effusion has significantly
decreased in size since thoracentesis without evidence of pneumothorax.  There
is subtotal but adequate re-expansion of the left lower lobe.  Moderate
cardiomegaly is unchanged.  The appearance of the aortic valve replacement and
median sternotomy wires is satisfactory.  The right lung is normal in
appearance.  High density material opacifies the stomach and large bowel, this
may represent contrast.

IMPRESSION:  
1. No evidence of pneumothorax after thoracentesis.
2. Residual small-to-moderate left pleural effusion.

CHEST

HISTORY:  Shoulder pain.  Thoracentesis.

Two views.  Comparison with the previous study done ___.  There is
interval development of increased density in the lower left chest consistent
with parenchymal consolidation.  There are small bilateral pleural effusions
as well.  Interstitial markings have increased somewhat.  The left heart
border is obscured.  The patient is status post median sternotomy and MVR, as
demonstrated on the earlier exam.  Mediastinal structures appear unchanged.

IMPRESSION:  Interval development of consolidation in the lower left chest. 
Small bilateral pleural effusions.  Increased interstitial markings consistent
with development of mild edema.

INDICATION:  Persistent left pleural effusion.

___ and ___.

TWO VIEWS OF THE CHEST:  Note is made of cardiomegaly, which is unchanged. 
Also unchanged are multiple mediastinotomy wires and a mitral valve
prosthesis.  As before, there is a left pleural effusion, with expected
overlying subsegmental atelectasis.  The volume of this effusion is increased.
There is also suggestion of a tiny right pleural effusion, a finding which is
new from the comparison study.  Additionally, the degree of pulmonary edema
has progressed.  There is no pneumothorax.
